contentBlocks.title: SASSA Grants for Caregivers — Grant-in-Aid, Child Support & More
contentBlocks.description: If you care for a child, elderly parent, or disabled family member, several SASSA grants can help. Learn about the Grant-in-Aid, Child Support Grant, and other financial support available to caregivers.

contentBlocks.text: If you are caring for a family member — whether a child, elderly parent, or disabled relative — you may qualify for several SASSA grants depending on your circumstances. SASSA provides specific grants to support caregivers, though the structure may not be what you expect.

Caring for a vulnerable family member is a significant financial and emotional responsibility. SASSA provides the Grant-in-Aid (for those caring for grant recipients who need 24-hour care) and the Child Support Grant (for primary caregivers of children). Understanding which grant applies to your specific caregiving situation is the first step to getting support.

Nomsa is a 38-year-old from Mthatha who cares for her elderly mother (who receives the Older Person Grant) and her two children aged 6 and 10. Her mother requires full-time care after a stroke. Nomsa's mother can apply for the Grant-in-Aid (R580/month top-up) because she needs 24-hour care. Nomsa herself can apply for the Child Support Grant (R580/month per child) for her two children. This means the household can receive up to R4,140 per month in total grants. This guide explains each option in detail.

rows: Person you care for must already receive a SASSA grant and have medical proof of needing 24-hour care.
Caregiver must meet the means test. Child must be under 18.
Medical proof of severe, permanent disability requiring full-time home care.

checklist: Must be a South African citizen or permanent resident
Must be the primary caregiver of the person needing care
Must have a valid South African ID
For Grant-in-Aid: the person you care for must already receive a SASSA grant
For Child Support Grant: the child must be under 18 and in your care
restrictions: Grant-in-Aid is paid to the grant recipient (the person receiving care), not the caregiver directly
Child Support Grant is means-tested for the caregiver's income
You cannot claim a caregiver's salary from SASSA — grants are designed to support the person receiving care, not pay the caregiver

documents.label: ID or birth certificate of the person you care for
Medical report confirming need for 24-hour care (for Grant-in-Aid)
Proof of income or affidavit of unemployment (for Child Support Grant means test)
Child's birth certificate (for Child Support Grant)

steps.title: Identify the right grant
steps.description: Determine which grant matches your caregiving situation: Grant-in-Aid for elderly/disabled care, Child Support Grant for children, or Foster Child Grant for foster children.

steps.title: Gather supporting documents
steps.description: Collect medical reports, IDs, birth certificates, and proof of income as required for your specific grant type.

steps.title: Visit your SASSA office
steps.description: Take all documents to your nearest SASSA office. Some grants (like Child Support) can be applied for at any time.

steps.title: Complete the application
steps.description: Fill in the application form with assistance from a SASSA officer. Ensure all details match your ID document.

contentBlocks.title: Understanding Grant-in-Aid
contentBlocks.text: Grant-in-Aid is often misunderstood. It is paid to the person receiving care (the grant beneficiary), not the caregiver. For example, if your elderly mother receives the Older Person Grant, she can apply for Grant-in-Aid to get an additional R580/month. This extra money helps cover care costs but is paid into her account, not yours.

items: Expecting Grant-in-Aid to be paid directly to you as a caregiver — it is paid to the grant recipient
Not applying for the Child Support Grant because you think only biological parents qualify — primary caregivers qualify
Assuming you cannot work while being a caregiver — you can receive grants and work if your income permits
Not getting a medical report for Grant-in-Aid — the doctor must specifically confirm that 24-hour care is needed

faqs.question: Can I get paid as a caregiver for looking after my elderly parent?
faqs.answer: Not directly. Your parent may qualify for the Grant-in-Aid on top of their Older Person Grant, but it is paid to them. You cannot claim a salary from SASSA for being a family caregiver.

faqs.question: Can I receive the Child Support Grant if I am not the biological parent?
faqs.answer: Yes. If you are the primary caregiver of the child (the person who meets the child's daily needs), you can apply for the Child Support Grant on behalf of the child.

faqs.question: Can I receive both Grant-in-Aid and Child Support Grant?
faqs.answer: Yes. They serve different purposes. The Child Support Grant is for a child in your care, while Grant-in-Aid is added to an older or disabled person's existing grant.

faqs.question: How does the medical assessment for Grant-in-Aid work?
faqs.answer: The person needing care must be assessed by a SASSA medical officer. The doctor must confirm they require full-time, 24-hour care from another person. A standard doctor's note is not sufficient.

faqs.question: Can I get the Care Dependency Grant if I care for a disabled child?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the child has a severe, permanent disability requiring full-time home care. The child must be assessed by a SASSA medical officer. The grant is R2,400 per month.
